lines.speaker: Charon
lines.text: Pay up, you little curse. Ferry fare.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Keep shouting, Charon, if it makes you happier.

lines.speaker: Charon
lines.text: I said pay me for carrying you across.
lines.description: more annoyed, repeating like a bill collector

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: You can’t collect from a man who hasn’t got it.

lines.speaker: Charon
lines.text: Is there such a thing as a man without one obol?

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Other men, I couldn’t say. I haven’t got one.

lines.speaker: Charon
lines.text: By Pluto, you filthy specimen, I’ll throttle you if you don’t pay.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: And I’ll take that pole of yours and crack your skull open.

lines.speaker: Charon
lines.text: So you made that whole trip for nothing, then.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Hermes can pay for me. He’s the one who handed me over.
lines.description: bright practical suggestion, passing the invoice along

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Oh yes, splendid. Now I’m subsidising the dead.

lines.speaker: Charon
lines.text: I’m not letting you go.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Fine. Haul the boat up and stand there forever on my account. But what I haven’t got—how exactly do you propose to take it?

lines.speaker: Charon
lines.text: You knew you were supposed to bring it.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: I knew. I didn’t have it. What then? Was I not supposed to die?
lines.description: crisp deadpan; final question lands dry

lines.speaker: Charon
lines.text: So you alone get to boast you sailed for free?

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Not free, my good man. I bailed water, I helped with the oar, and unlike every other passenger, I didn’t spend the crossing crying.
lines.description: reasonable, listing services; last clause lightly cutting

lines.speaker: Charon
lines.text: None of that counts with a ferryman. You owe the obol. Procedure does not allow alternatives.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Then take me back to life.

lines.speaker: Charon
lines.text: Very funny. And pick up a beating from Aeacus for my trouble.
lines.description: sour, knows he has lost the practical argument

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Then stop bothering me.

lines.speaker: Charon
lines.text: Show me what you’ve got in the bag.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Lupins, if you want them. And Hecate’s leftovers.

lines.speaker: Charon
lines.text: Hermes, where did you find this dog? And the things he said all the way across—laughing at every passenger, needling them, and singing by himself while the rest of them wailed.
lines.description: exasperated complaint, building into grievance report

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: You don’t know whom you ferried, Charon? A genuinely free man. He doesn’t care about anything. That’s Menippus.
lines.description: warmly amused, admiring but still managerial

lines.speaker: Charon
lines.text: Well, if I ever get hold of you again—

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: If you get hold of me, my good man. But you won’t get hold of me twice.
lines.description: delighted final parry, dry and absolute
